author.name: Automation Alex
author.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.

challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: I am fine with running the shadow model in a governed environment to verify the new allocation logic before we touch the live forecast. However, I will not approve any changes to the existing CI/CD pipeline configuration. If the shadow setup requires me to modify the current deployment scripts or add new automated triggers, I am stepping back from the project. I am willing to accept a fully manual process for the shadow run, including manual data loading and result verification, provided it keeps the main pipeline stable and untouched. I am giving up the convenience of automated shadow testing to ensure the core infrastructure remains reliable and unbroken during this critical promotion week.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are giving up the convenience of automated shadow testing to ensure the core infrastructure remains stable, which fits the definition of a trade-off where something is accepted as a loss.
